The response is correct. The tap fills 1/3 of the tank per hour and the drain empties 1/5 per hour, so the net rate is 1/3 − 1/5 = 2/15 per hour. The tank therefore fills in 15/2 = 7.5 hours, which matches the stated answer. It shows the key reasoning (the rates and their subtraction) concisely and clearly, and it stays well under 120 words. The only minor gap is that it doesn't note the assumption that the drain's rate applies while the tank is filling, but that is the standard reading of the problem.
